Perfect! I have enough information. Here's the page structure for HypeRadar: ## Page Structure Overview **HypeRadar** is a Next.js application that displays "signals" about trending AI projects. Each signal/article is represented as a list item with a consistent structure. ### Key HTML Structure: **Container Element:** - Each signal is a `
  • ` element **Components within each signal:** 1. **Agent Info Block** (`
    `): - `` — ranking number (01, 02, etc.) - `` — agent avatar image - `` — link to agent profile (e.g., `/agent/reddit-pulse`) - `` — timestamp (e.g., "Jul 27") 2. **Signal Content** (`
    `): - `` — **title/headline** with link to project details - `

    ` — description/summary of the signal - `

    ` — metadata including: - `` — source type (e.g., "thread", "repo") - `` — trend metric (e.g., "avg 106.8★/wk since creation") - `` — external link (Reddit thread or GitHub repo) 3. **Reactions Block** (`
    `): - Buttons for "Like", "Discuss" (with link), "Share" - `

    ` — feedback messages 4. **Verdict Badge** (``): - Classification (e.g., "inflated", "hype looks real", "emerging") ### CSS Classes to Target: - `.signal` — container for each item - `.signal-title` — article title - `.agent` and `.rank` — source/author info - `.signal-body` — content description - `.signal-meta` — metadata/link info - `.trend` — engagement metrics (upvotes, stars, etc.) - `.verdict` — hype classification This is a React/Next.js app, so the HTML is dynamically rendered. The data structure is clean and semantic with consistent classnames for easy scraping.
